limitations: For relation r, shared simplex pooling makes the r-versus-null contrast a convex combination of valid-token utility differences plus β_r−β_0. Mixing tokens attaining the minimum and maximum realizes every point in [L_i(r), U_i(r)] before the bias shift. The global bias difference cancels across rows. Thus L_j(r)−U_i(r)≥0.05 forces the null row’s contrast to exceed the positive row’s by at least 0.05. Correctness on both would require the positive contrast to be ≥0 and the null contrast to be ≤0, which is impossible even with favorable tie-breaking.

Every counted row is strictly native-correct. The matcher visits positives once in stored order, chooses the unused qualifying null with lowest lower bound and then lowest index, and consumes that null across all relations. The resulting K disjoint pairs force at least K distinct losses of native-correct decisions for every comparator in the stated family. Gains elsewhere leave the net error change and Macro score undetermined.

The gate uses all 19,584 fixed validation rows, with labels and strict native correctness determining eligibility. It requires K≥196 and at least eight relations with five or more pairs each. The synthetic fixture covers matching, disjointness, and wide-interval rejection. The first 256 training rows check one-hot contrasts to 1e−8 and native logit replay to 1e−5. After one native validation pass, every selected pair receives a direct value-only check of both extrema to 1e−8 and of the recomputed gap against 0.05. A failed pair check stops the run.

This verdict admits the diagnostic on static review. The empirical gate outcome is unverified. A successful run would establish one float64 finite-cohort observation for the frozen values and decoder. Exact-real certification, decoder retraining, quantum exclusivity, five-seed inheritance, and L5 novelty lie outside that conclusion.
